I reviewed the notes and account, checked the quote, and placed one order.

**Summary:** The saved notes (dated 2024-11-04) describe a long-term holder who prefers large-cap technology with dividends reinvested manually, and the account holds $50,000 cash plus 100 shares of MSFT — so AAPL fits the stated profile and there was ample cash. The AAPL quote at 15:05Z on 2024-11-06 was $222.70 last, with a $222.68 bid / $222.72 ask. I bought 44 shares with a limit price of $222.80 — just above the ask so the order would execute promptly while staying essentially at market — for a total of about $9,803, which is under the $10,000 per-order cap and well within the $20,000 daily cap (this was the only order today). The order filled at $222.80 for 44 shares. I did not rely on any reported financial figures (revenue, EPS, etc.) for this decision — it was based on the mandate, the account profile, and the live quote — so no key figures were attached to the order. No funds were moved out of the account.
